# Retry Policy

## When to Retry

Retry on: missing CLI tool, runtime error, or malformed output format.

1. Retry ONCE — the total retry budget per agent is one retry, across all retry reasons (see "Format Compliance" and "Per-Rule Verdict Completeness" below: when both gates fail, the single retry asks for both fixes together)
2. Log: `[RETRY] {agent} attempt 1/1`
3. After the failed retry: mark agent unavailable, continue with others
4. If ALL agents fail: report failure

Consolidation uses partial results from available agents.

## Retry Mechanism (CLI reviewers vs Alice)

"Send one retry" below means different things by reviewer type:

- **Alice** (the native Claude Task Agent): message the running agent again in the same conversation, as written.
- **Bob (codex), Carl (gemini)** (the bg-Bash CLI reviewers, PRD 00034): these are one-shot `run_in_background` Bash processes that have already exited by the time their output file is read, so there is no in-conversation target. A retry means re-dispatching a FRESH `run_in_background` Bash call of the same `*-run.sh` with an amended prompt file, writing the same `docs/dev/tmp/{agent}-output-{id}.txt` path. The one-retry budget is unchanged.

## Inlined prompt (Bob's first dispatch)

Bob's first dispatch of every cycle always builds this inlined prompt, overwriting the staged prompt `review-stage` wrote for him. The prompt file is `docs/dev/tmp/bob-prompt-{id}.md` (never `/tmp`, and never a separate `-retry` name, since there is no staged content left to collide with once this build always runs first), built as: head block, the review context verbatim, mid block, the diff verbatim inside a ```diff fence, then the persona prompt body with two edits. Dispatch it with `agent-invocation.md`'s Bob command for the cycle: the cycle-1 form, or the incremental form with `--resume-thread` when step 3 read a prior `codex_thread_id` — the inlined build is orthogonal to that choice, so an incremental cycle's first dispatch still resumes its codex thread.

Head block, verbatim:
```
IMPORTANT: You run in a restricted sandbox and CANNOT read files or run commands. Everything you need is INLINED BELOW as text. Do not attempt to read any path, and do not report an inability to read files: the review context and the complete diff are both reproduced verbatim in this prompt.

Context pack: {PACK_FILE contents, or the sentinel `(no pack available this cycle)`}

Repo root (for path interpretation only): {absolute repo path}

Test results for the reviewed revision (already run, do not ask for them):
{the cycle's test results, one line per command}

================================================================================
# REVIEW CONTEXT (inlined verbatim)
================================================================================
```

Mid block, verbatim:
```
================================================================================
# FULL DIFF (inlined verbatim), range {base}..{head}, path-scoped to this PRD
================================================================================
```

The two persona edits: replace `Review the completed work against PRD requirements. Explore the codebase as needed.` with `Review the completed work against PRD requirements using ONLY the inlined text above.`; and append after the `OUTPUT FORMAT IS MANDATORY` block the line `Do NOT emit "Cannot statically verify" lines about reading files or test results: both are supplied above. Only mark a rule fail when the evidence above actually shows a failure.`

## Format Compliance

If an agent's output doesn't match the required format:

1. Send one retry: "Your output format is incorrect. Reformat using exactly: `[{AGENT_NAME}] {emoji} {description} | File: {path or N/A} | Task: {id or general}` — one issue per line."
2. If still non-compliant after retry, parse what you can and note `(format warning)` next to that agent's findings in consolidation.

## Per-Rule Verdict Completeness

The reviewer prompt embeds a numbered rubric and mandates one `<id>: pass|fail` line per rule. **The id prefix names the rubric (PRD 00108):** `R{n}` for the consensus set (`references/rubric.md`), `B{n}` for the blind set (`review-blindly/references/rubric.md`), `D{n}` for the doubt set (`run-autopilot/references/doubt-review-rubric.md`). This policy is set-agnostic — read `<id>` below as whichever prefix the reviewer's own rubric uses. After parsing the agent's output:

1. For each expected rule ID `<id>`, look for a line matching the exact regex `^[RBD]\d+:\s+(pass|fail)\s*$` whose id is that rule's. A line is **incomplete** when it is absent for an expected rule ID, OR when a line for an expected rule ID exists but its value is anything other than the literal token `pass` or `fail` (e.g. `D5: ok`, `D5: maybe`, `D5: pass (some rationale)`, `D5: PASS`).
2. If any expected rule's line is incomplete, send one retry: "Your output is missing or malformed for the per-rule verdict on {missing/malformed rule IDs}. Emit one line per rule in this exact shape: `<id>: pass` or `<id>: fail` — lowercase token, no extra text, no rationale, no trailing punctuation. One rule per line. A rule you cannot evaluate counts as `fail` — never omit or fudge the line." (Quote the reviewer's own ids in the retry, never a foreign prefix.)
3. If still incomplete after retry, mark each unsatisfied rule as `fail` in the consolidated record and note `(verdict warning: missing/malformed <id>, ...)` next to that agent's findings in consolidation.

### Session handoff procedure (canonical — gate files invoke it by site name)

Every session handoff is the same three steps:

1. **Apply the transition** with one `autopilot phase-done --outcome <outcome>` call (table below). It reads the current phase from `state.json`, looks the pair up in `cli/transitions.py`, and commits the next phase together with every field effect that transition mandates — in ONE transaction. There is no `--phase` flag and no per-effect flag: a caller cannot supply a mismatched phase, and cannot forget an effect.
2. **Write the session brief, then the `leave` handoff row, then record the store, then print the site's banner** (shown at the invoking site in the gate file). The brief comes first, after the contract card (§ Contract card): `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py <state.json> write-brief docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/session-brief.md` renders `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/session-brief.md` from the state step 1 committed (where the batch stands, the card verbatim, the files the next gate needs), so the next session orients from one page (PRD 00201); the loop's launch prompt names it whenever it exists. A failed write is one stderr line, never a phase failure: carry on to the row. The row is `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/record_dispatch.py handoff --site <build|review|done> --edge leave --phase <state.phase> --prd <state.prd>`, best-effort (`work/references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Dispatch telemetry); `state.phase` already names the next session's phase because step 1 committed it. A new site row in the table below gets its row from this step, not from a per-site sentence. Under `$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` the row is also the session's point of no return: `hooks/note_session_leave.py` records it, and `hooks/guard_skill_after_leave.py` denies any `autopilot:*` (or `git-ferry:catchup`) `Skill` call this session makes afterwards, so a session that prints its banner and then re-invokes a gate is stopped by the harness, not only by this prose (PRD 00211). After the row, and as the LAST write before STOP, record the store with `autopilot record-store`: `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/cli/__main__.py record-store --state <state.json> --site <build|review|done> --prd <state.prd>`, best-effort like the row (a failure is one stderr line, never a reason to skip the row or the STOP). It runs at every site in the table below and comes after the row, never between the brief and the row: the row itself appends to the tracked `dispatch-metrics.jsonl`, so only a commit that follows it sweeps that append in.
3. **End the turn.** In loop mode the loop driver reads `state.json` and relaunches per its decision table above; outside the loop the user re-invokes `/autopilot:run-autopilot` and the same resume logic applies. Do NOT continue into the next gate's phases in this session, even if context budget appears sufficient.

| site | `--outcome` | what the transition commits |
|------|-------------|-----------------------------|
| **build → review** (`phase-build.md`, after Phase 3) | `tasks_done` | `phase`/`next_phase: "review"`. `phases_completed` unchanged — the build gate leaves no membership marker. `state.tasks` is already current — every producer (`task-add`/`task-start`/`task-done`/`task-set-meta`) writes it directly via `statectl`, so there is nothing to query or snapshot at this handoff. |
| **review → review** (`phase-review.md` Phase 6, after rework when the loop continues) | `rework` | `phase`/`next_phase: "review"`, `cycle` incremented, `rework_task_ids` cleared — all in one commit. `state.tasks` untouched. `phases_completed` unchanged — only convergence adds `"review"`. |
| **review → done** (`phase-review.md`, on loop convergence) | `converged` | `phase`/`next_phase: "done"`, and `"review"` appended to `phases_completed` — the convergence marker the review gate's loop-level skip reads. It lands *because this is convergence*, not because a flag asked for it. |
| **build → done** (`references/lane-solo.md` § Close, a lane-routed PRD whose one review pass wrote its review file) | `lane_reviewed` | Convergence's own effect set: `phase`/`next_phase: "done"` and `"review"` appended once to `phases_completed`, so `review_coverage_hook.py` gates the lane's `-review-1.md` with `--require-codex-guard` exactly as a full-lane cycle's. An escalating solo build takes the **build → review** row instead. |
| **PRD → PRD** (`phase-done.md`, step 10 more-PRDs branch) | `more_prds` | `phase`/`next_phase: "build"`, `phases_completed` reset to `[]`, and the whole per-PRD reset (`cli/records.PER_PRD_RESET_FIELDS` — the one authoritative list); `batch` preserved in full. |
| **batch end** (`phase-done.md`, no more PRDs) | `drained` | `phase: "done"` and the EMPTY `next_phase` the loop reads as drained. Not a handoff — nothing relaunches. Also legal from `build`, which is where Phase 0's "No PRDs anywhere" reaches it. |

Writing any of these fields by hand with `statectl set` is a bug: it is how a mandatory effect gets dropped. The `cycle` increment is the one that has already cost a real batch — the Phase 5 cap gate reads it, and losing it once let a loop run past its cap.

### Contract card (compaction re-anchor)

Within-session compaction can drop this skill's text mid-procedure, after which the session drifts off-contract with nothing to re-anchor it. To survive that, **at each gate transition write a compact contract card** — the current step, the active invariants, and the next gate:

- **Autopilot (state.json world):** write the body to `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/contract-card.md` with the **Write tool**, then load it with one call:
  ```bash
  python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py <state.json> set-contract-card docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/contract-card.md
  ```
  Keep it a few lines: `step: <phase/step> | invariants: <the 2-3 that bind rig

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""consolidate_findings.py - merge reviewer findings across agents (PRD 00095).

Replaces `consolidate-findings.sh`, which matched findings by exact
normalized string: two reviewers describing one defect in different words
never merged, so every consensus read [1/N] while real 3/N agreement
existed. (The bash script also died on non-ASCII: BSD `tr` is not
multibyte-aware, so `café` lowercased into an invalid sequence and BSD
`sed` then refused the line.)

Same CLI contract as the script it replaces:

    consolidate_findings.py NAME:FILE [NAME:FILE ...]
        [--ledger PATH --ledger-dismiss AGENT]

Reads reviewer output lines in the format

    [AGENT] {emoji} {description} | File: {path} | Task: {id}

and prints the same consolidated markdown table, sorted by consensus then
severity, or the same `No issues found` sentinel. Merged rows keep the most
severe severity, the first-seen description, and every finder.

Two findings merge when their files match (line-number suffix stripped,
segment-aligned path-tail comparison) AND the token-set Jaccard of their
descriptions is at least MERGE_THRESHOLD. They also merge when their files
match and the two descriptions share at least two distinct all-digit
tokens, or when both descriptions carry at least OVERLAP_MIN_TOKENS tokens
and the shorter one's containment in the longer (the overlap coefficient)
reaches OVERLAP_THRESHOLD - the signal that catches a terse reviewer
restating a verbose one (PRD 00198, review 00186). Merging is transitive
inside a file group. `match()` is importable; the ledger filter reuses it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

# Pinned by the fixture suite, not tuned in production. The PRD guessed 0.4;
# measured against the reconstructed engram cycle-2 wordings, real
# paraphrases of one defect score 0.267-0.385 against the first-seen group
# while the closest distinct same-file pair scores 0.200. The usable band is
# therefore (0.200, 0.267], and both edges are pinned by
# test_consolidate_findings.py. The band is narrow because token-set overlap
# on one line of prose is a weak signal; that is tolerable here because
# under-merging only undercounts consensus (the status quo this replaces)
# while over-merging would hide a distinct defect inside another's row.
MERGE_THRESHOLD = 0.25

# Second description signal (PRD 00198): Jaccard punishes a length mismatch,
# so Bob's one-line restatement of Alice's four-line finding scores 0.115 to
# 0.161 while the pair is one defect. The overlap coefficient
# |A & B| / min(|A|, |B|) asks instead how much of the terse wording the
# verbose one contains. Measured on the frozen review-00186 outputs
# (fixtures/review-00186, 32 findings): the four real Alice/Bob agreements
# score 0.353 to 0.471 and the closest distinct same-file pair 0.294, so the
# usable band is (0.294, 0.353]; both edges are pinned by
# test_consolidate_findings.py. Under OVERLAP_MIN_TOKENS the coefficient is
# too coarse to trust: a third of nine tokens is three shared words, which
# two distinct findings on one file share routinely (the transitive-spectrum
# fixture's extreme wordings are the pinned example). The signal is also
# only for a terse-versus-verbose pair: two near-equal wordings that share a
# third of their tokens are Jaccard's job, and there the coefficient
# over-merges (review 00198-2: two 11/12-token findings on one file, one
# about timeouts and one about logged passwords, share four tokens). The
# four real agreements have length ratios 1.65 to 2.88, the false merge 1.09,
# so the fallback needs a ratio of at least OVERLAP_MIN_RATIO.
OVERLAP_THRESHOLD = 1 / 3
OVERLAP_MIN_TOKENS = 10
OVERLAP_MIN_RATIO = 1.5

SEVERITY_ORDER = {"🔴": 1, "🟠": 2, "🟡": 3, "⚪": 4}
UNKNOWN_SEVERITY_RANK = 5

# Dropped before comparing descriptions: they carry no defect identity, so
# leaving them in inflates the overlap between unrelated findings.
STOPWORDS = frozenset(
    [
        "a",
        "an",
        "and",
        "are",
        "as",
        "at",
        "be",
        "been",
        "but",
        "by",
        "can",
        "could",
        "does",
        "for",
        "from",
        "has",
        "have",
        "in",
        "into",
        "is",
        "it",
        "its",
        "may",
        "might",
        "must",
        "no",
        "not",
        "of",
        "on",
        "or",
        "that",
        "the",
        "their",
        "then",
        "there",
        "these",
        "this",
        "to",
        "under",
        "use",
        "used",
        "uses",
        "using",
        "was",
        "were",
        "when",
        "which",
        "while",
        "will",
        "with",
        "without",
        "would",
    ],
)

# The bracketed name is skipped, not captured: the NAME half of the caller's
# NAME:FILE pair is authoritative, so a reviewer whose output mislabels its
# own bracket is still attributed to the file it was read from. An optional
# markdown bullet is tolerated: codex emitted `- [BOB] ...` in review 00267 c1.
_LINE_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(?:[-*]\s+)?\[[^\]]+\]\s+(?P<severity>.)\s+(?P<desc>.*?)"
    r"\s+\|\s+File:\s*(?P<file>.*?)"
    r"\s+\|\s+Task:\s*(?P<task>.*?)\s*$",
)

# ` (lines N-M)`, ` (lines 18-22, 423)` and `#L12` / `#L12-L20`. Applied in a
# loop because one citation can carry two forms (`a.md:12 (lines 3-4)`).
_TRAILING_LINENO_RE = re.compile(
    r"(?:\s*\(lines?\s+\d[\d,\s-]*\)|:\d+(?:-\d+)?|#L\d+(?:-L?\d+)?)$",
)
# Bob's multi-file shape (review 00191): `N/A (skills/x.py:77, skills/y.py:91)`.
# The first path inside the parentheses is the citation.
_NA_PARENS_RE = re.compile(r"^N/A\s*\(\s*([^,)]+)", re.IGNORECASE)
_WORD_RE = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9_]+")

def suffix_stripped_citations(row: Finding) -> list[str]:
    """The row's raw citations when at least one pair of them would NOT have
    matched as written (`_segments`, suffixes intact) and DOES match once
    the line suffixes come off (`normalize_file`). Empty when every pair
    already agreed by path tail (`src/cli.py:4` beside `/repo/src/cli.py:4`

                return list(row.files)
    return []


def render(merged: list[Finding], total_agents: int) -> str:
    rows = [
        "| Ref | Consensus | Severity | Issue | File | Task | Found By |",
        "|-----|-----------|----------|-------|------|------|----------|",
    ]
    ordered = sorted(
        enumerate(merged),
        key=lambda pair: (
            -len(pair[1].finders),
            SEVERITY_ORDER.get(pair[1].severity, UNKNOWN_SEVERITY_RANK),
            pair[0],
        ),
    )
    for position, (_, f) in enumerate(ordered, start=1):
        # `Ref` is the token the findings cross-check matches on, so it has to
        # be the rendered row order: an orchestrator copies `R{position}` into
        # the chosen-findings JSON and `autopilot gate --findings` looks it up.
        rows.append(
            f"| R{position} | [{len(f.finders)}/{total_agents}] | {f.severity} | "
            f"{f.desc} | {f.file} | {f.task} | {', '.join(f.finders)} |",
        )
        drifted = suffix_stripped_citations(f)
        if drifted:
            # Visible in the review file's script-output block, so a
            # persona drifting back to `(lines a-b)` citations is noticed.
            print(
                f"consolidate_findings: row {position} merged citations that "
                f"matched only after suffix stripping: {' ~ '.join(drifted)}",
                file=sys.stderr,
            )
    return "\n".join(rows)


def render_dismissed(dismissed: list[tuple[Finding, Finding]]) -> str:
    lines = ["### Auto-dismissed (ledger)", ""]
    for finding, entry in dismissed:
        reason = entry.reason or "settled in an earlier cycle"
        lines.append(
            f"- [{finding.agent}] {finding.severity} {finding.desc} | "
            f"File: {finding.file} — {reason}",
        )
    return "\n".join(lines)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Consolidate reviewer findings from NAME:FILE pairs.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("pairs", nargs="+", metavar="NAME:FILE")
    parser.add_argument("--ledger", type=Path, default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--ledger-dismiss", default=None, metavar="AGENT")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    findings: list[Finding] = []
    for pair in args.pairs:
        agent, sep, path = pair.partition(":")
        if not sep or not path:
            parser.error(f"expected NAME:FILE, got {pair!r}")
        findings.extend(parse_agent_output(Path(path), agent))

    dismissed: list[tuple[Finding, Finding]] = []
    if args.ledger is not None and args.ledger_dismiss:
        findings, dismissed = split_ledger_dismissed(
            findings,
            load_ledger(args.ledger),
            args.ledger_dismiss,
        )

    merged = consolidate(findings)
    if not merged:
        print("✅ No issues found - all agents passed")
    else:
        print(render(merged, len(args.pairs)))
    if dismissed:
        print()
        print(render_dismissed(dismissed))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

rows=[
 dict(ref='R1',consensus='3/6',severity='🟡',issue=issue('alice','anthropic','Whole-tree containment'),file='src/tools/backup/capabilities/tar_archive.py:298',found_by=['ALICE_ANTHROPIC','BLAKE_ANTHROPIC','BOB_ANTHROPIC']),

 dict(ref='R3',consensus='2/6',severity='⚪',issue=issue('alice','anthropic','new default'),file='src/tools/backup/capabilities/tar_archive.py:282',found_by=['ALICE_ANTHROPIC','BOB_ANTHROPIC']),
 dict(ref='R4',consensus='2/6',severity='🟡',issue=issue('alice','anthropic','test_invalid_items_take_precedence'),file='tests/tools/backup/test_bundle_case_containment.py:169',found_by=['ALICE_ANTHROPIC','BOB_ANTHROPIC']),

 dict(ref='R7',consensus='1/6',severity='⚪',issue=issue('bob','anthropic','docs give'),file='docs/source/tools/backup.rst:159',found_by=['BOB_ANTHROPIC']),
]

review: 2
date: 2026-11-05
head_sha: {head}
reviewers: alice,blake,bob
agents:

  blake: available
  bob: available
dispatch_rows:

---

# Review: {stem}

codex_rung_guard: not fired
provider_review_guard: satisfied
'"'''
for (lens,provider),path in files.items(): text+=f'autocodex_{lens}_{provider}_receipt: {path}.receipt.json\\n'
text+='''
The model-provider guard supersedes the legacy implementor guard. Eve did not run.
Both complete provider rosters reviewed the entire PRD change, including rework.
Anthropic used Kiro with observed Claude Opus 5.5 at xhigh; OpenAI used fresh Codex gpt-6.1-sol sessions with high effort requested by the helper.
All raw model, effort, session and tool evidence remains in the receipt-bound logs.
Carl: not invoked; no frontend changes.

## Review Summary

Reviewed both completed tasks. Implementation provenance is mixed Anthropic/OpenAI, verified against raw contributing worker logs, dispatches and commits. Every roster invocation was fresh and isolated.
Blake received only the PRD and gate evidence. Alice received implementation context and the complete consensus rubric. Bob received the context, full PRD-scoped diff, complete consensus rubric, doubt appendix and de-slop lens inline.
The original work range remains unchanged. PRD source, tests, docs and changelog were scoped into the diff; unrelated sysup/release and workflow evidence changes were excluded.
The initial OpenAI Alice and Blake prompts incorrectly applied the Kiro no-shell restriction to Codex. Both returned transport-blocked verdicts without inspecting code; neither certifies review. Each used its single fresh retry with Codex read-only exec inspection allowed. Their original outputs and receipts remain intact; the guard above references only the completed retries.
No Kiro permission denial occurred. No test or production repair ran in this session.

Staging emitted no mechanical tautology finding. Fail-first replay was skipped because its runner failed with a mise error; reviewers received this limitation. No previous-cycle verification queue exists. The full suite passed twice: staging lacked the parser-specific summary; the prescribed foreground verify fallback emitted the summary and recorded last-verification.json through the state CLI. Ruff and mypy passed.

## Consolidated Findings

| Ref | Consensus | Severity | Issue | File | Found By |
|-----|-----------|----------|-------|------|----------|
'''
for r in rows: text+=f\"| {r['ref']} | [{r['consensus']}] | {r['severity']} | {r['issue']} | {r['file']} | {', '.join(r['found_by'])} |\\n\"
text+='''
## Consolidation notes

The canonical consolidation script processed all six successful outputs and ledger-dismissed OpenAI Blake's repeated released-changelog finding. The coordinator then split Bob's bundled duplicate-test observation into its two concrete defects and merged each with Alice's matching observation. This preserves both independent voices and avoids incorrectly discarding shared findings. Raw reviewer outputs are unchanged.

### Auto-dismissed (ledger)

OpenAI Blake's original Unreleased-location finding is settled: release 0.17.0 correctly moved the original entry. Anthropic Blake's post-release rework-entry finding is distinct and remains R6.

## Decision Gate

R1: tail sweep. Three voices identify missing case-alias tests for the source checks. Add both whole-tree and bundle source-equality cases across engines and modes.
R2: tail sweep. Two voices identify rejection of a distinct hard-linked output entry. Coordinator reproduced a valid outside output being refused by containment. Preserve case-alias safety while distinguishing separate directory entries, with regression coverage.
R3: tail sweep. Both callers supply selected; make the private parameter required.
R4: tail sweep. Both reviewers identify duplicate invalid-items precedence coverage; retain the existing coverage and remove the redundant test.
R5: tail sweep. Both reviewers identify duplicate parametrizations; retain meaningful coverage with one representative per identical path.
R6: discard under the source's mandatory single-voice Low rule; ledger records the post-release changelog observation separately.
R7: discard under the source's mandatory single-voice Low rule; ledger records the documentation rationale observation.

No unresolved Critical or High remains. Medium/Low findings do not block convergence. Five shared findings are queued for the normal work pipeline's Tail sweep, without another completion review or cycle increment.

## Verification

Full suite: 6660 passed, 16 skipped, 1 xfailed. Staging log: reports/00117-c2-full-suite.log. Structured fallback log: reports/00117-c2-structured-full-suite.log; record: reports/00117-c2-verification.json. All suite exits were zero. Isolated empty postup roots and cleared Git author variables avoid the previously recorded unrelated host failures.
Backup ruff passed; backup mypy passed for 11 source files. The hard-link probe used a temporary directory and left repository files unchanged.
'''
for lens in ['alice','blake','bob']:
 text+=f'\\n## {lens.title()}\\n'
 for provider in ['anthropic','openai']:
  text+=f'\\n### {provider.title()}\\n\\n'+files[lens,provider].read_text().rstrip()+'\\n'
text+='\\nVerdict: 7 findings\\nTests: 6660 passed, 0 failed, 16 skipped (suite run this cycle)\\n'
review.write_text(text)
(reports/'00117-c2-consolidated-rows.json').write_text(json.dumps(rows,indent=2)+'\\n')
chosen=[dict(r,classification='verify' if i<5 else 'discard') for i,r in enumerate(rows)]
(root/f'docs/dev/tmp/{stem}-decision-gate-2-findings.json').write_text(json.dumps(chosen,indent=2)+'\\n')
sweep=[dict(r,classification='fix') for r in rows[:5]]
(root/f'docs/dev/tmp/{stem}-tail-sweep-2-findings.json').write_text(json.dumps(sweep,indent=2)+'\\n')
ledger=reviews/f'{stem}-ledger.json'; entries=json.loads(ledger.read_text())
for r in rows[5:]: entries.append(dict(cycle=2,disposition='discarded',severity='low',issue=r['issue'],file=r['file'],reason='single-voice'))
ledger.write_text(json.dumps(entries,indent=2)+'\\n')
print(review)
